topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states its learning objectives before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Genetic evolution and susceptibility to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate in susceptible cells and enable cancer to evolve within a permissive environment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than treating cancer as an inevitable consequence of bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and their host environment.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens generate DNA damage and mutations, including the role of metabolism in determining their activity.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why tumour development can require a promoter that enables previously initiated cells to proliferate.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics place tissue- and life-stage-dependent susceptibility within the broader account of how DNA damage leads to cancer.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from people and their tumours can link particular exposures to cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
